Implement tamper-evident append-only audit log with hash-chain sealing for security and delegation events.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/security/audit.py (distinct from backend/memory/audit.py — security/delegation events only)
- Define AuditEntry model: timestamp, event_type, actor_id, resource, payload_hash, prev_hash, entry_hash
- Implement AuditLogWriter.append() — computes SHA-256 chain: entry_hash = sha256(prev_hash + canonical_json)
- Implement verify_audit_chain(entries) -> bool for tamper detection
- Persist to PostgreSQL audit_log table via Alembic migration 006_audit_log_sealed
- Log events: credential_issued, credential_revoked, consent_granted, guardrail_violation, delegation_created
- Add audit_log_entries_total and audit_chain_verification_failures_total Prometheus metrics
- Integrate writer calls from consent flow and (stub for Day 4) credential broker
- Document in docs/SECURITY.md § Cryptographic Audit Integrity

EFFORT: L (8 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend, Security
DEPENDENCIES: DB-122

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Append 3 entries; verify_audit_chain returns True
- Tamper middle entry_hash; verify_audit_chain returns False
- audit_log_entries_total increments on append
- Tests in backend/tests/security/test_audit_sealing.py pass (≥8 scenarios)

EDGE CASES:
- First entry: prev_hash = genesis constant (64 zero hex chars)
- Concurrent appends: use DB serial or row-level lock to preserve chain order
- Payload contains PII: store payload_hash only, not raw payload in audit row
- Empty chain verify: return True (no entries to tamper)
- Migration on existing DB: audit_log table created idempotently

Implement CredentialBroker for Just-In-Time short-lived credential issuance to MCP clients.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/security/vault.py with Credential, CredentialBroker classes
- Broker.get_credential(user_id, service, intent, ttl_seconds=900) interface per proposal v2.0.0
- Services: google_calendar, supabase (read_tasks, read_events, update_tasks intents)
- Validate user consent before issuance (reuse consent_records lookup)
- Dev mode: in-memory TTL cache (dict + expiry); prod-ready interface for Redis/Vault swap
- Retrieve long-lived refresh token from settings/env; exchange for short-lived access token
- Log every issuance via backend/security/audit.py AuditLogWriter
- Add credential_issuance_total{service,intent} Prometheus metric
- Update backend/mcp/calendar_stdio.py to request credentials via broker instead of raw env refresh token
- Add VAULT_MODE setting: env | memory (default env for backward compat during migration)
- Document in docs/SECURITY.md § JIT Credential Issuance and .env.example VAULT_* vars

EFFORT: L (8 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend, Security
DEPENDENCIES: DB-123

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Broker returns credential with expires_at within TTL
- Expired credential rejected on second get within TTL window uses cache
- Consent missing: raises CredentialDeniedError, no token issued
- credential_issuance_total increments per service
- Tests in backend/tests/security/test_vault.py pass (≥10 scenarios)
- Calendar MCP client uses broker in test with mocked token exchange

EDGE CASES:
- TTL=0 or negative: raise ValueError before issuance
- User_id mismatch on consent: deny issuance
- Token exchange failure: audit log + raise CredentialBrokerError, no partial token returned
- Broker called twice same second: cache hit, single audit entry (idempotent within TTL)
- GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN unset: clear error directing to OAuth setup guide
